title: Review: Chemistry — Atoms, elements and compounds
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C2#c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C2.2#xt2 term and clue written for the game; C2.4#xt1 term and clue written for the game; C2#c15 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: C2#q21, C2#q09, C2#q12, C2#q16, C2#q01, C2#q06, C2#q13, C2#x03 (written for the game), C2#x01 (written for the game), C2#q07, C2#q15, C2#q19. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atom
items.clue: The smallest particle of an element that can exist.

items.label: Chemical symbol
items.clue: One or two letters that stand for an element, such as O or Mg

items.label: Mass
items.clue: The amount of matter in an object, measured in grams or kilograms

items.label: Dissolving
items.clue: A solid spreads out as separate particles among those of a liquid.

questions.stem: In Dalton's model, what happens if you keep cutting a piece of copper into smaller and smaller bits?

options.text: You can keep cutting smaller bits for ever
You reach tiny orange, bendy copper atoms
You reach atoms that cannot be split
You reach atoms visible in a light microscope

questions.explanation: Yes. In Dalton's model, matter is made of tiny atoms that cannot be broken down. Cutting stops at single copper atoms.

questions.stem: Hydrogen burns, and oxygen helps things burn. They react to make water, which does neither. What does this show?

options.text: The atoms were destroyed in the reaction
The atoms changed into new water atoms
Water has too little hydrogen to burn
A new substance with its own properties formed

questions.explanation: Yes. Water is a compound, a new substance whose properties are different from those of hydrogen and oxygen. The atoms are the same ones, now joined in a new way.

questions.stem: Methane has the formula CH₄. How many atoms are in one molecule of methane?

options.text: 2 atoms
4 atoms
5 atoms
8 atoms

questions.explanation: Yes. C with no number means one carbon atom, and H₄ means four hydrogen atoms: 1 + 4 = 5.

questions.stem: Some ice in a sealed bag melts, and a little of the water evaporates. What happens to the mass of the bag and its contents?

options.text: It goes down, as liquids weigh less than solids
It stays the same, as no particles are lost
It goes up, as ice floats, so water is heavier
It goes down, as water vapour weighs nothing

questions.explanation: Yes. Melting and evaporating are changes of state: the same water particles are there, just arranged differently. Nothing gets into or out of the sealed bag, so the mass stays the same.

questions.stem: Which idea is part of Dalton's atomic model?

options.text: An atom has the colour of its element
Atoms can be seen with a light microscope
All atoms of one element are identical
Atoms are destroyed when things burn

questions.explanation: Yes. In Dalton's model every atom of one element is the same, and atoms of different elements are different (they have different masses). He also said atoms cannot be broken down, made or destroyed.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of every molecule?

options.text: It contains atoms of two different elements
It is two or more atoms joined together
It is just another word for an atom
It can be seen with a light microscope

questions.explanation: Yes. A molecule is two or more atoms joined (bonded) together. The atoms can be the same, as in O₂, or different, as in H₂O.

questions.stem: What does the formula N₂ show?

options.text: Two nitrogen atoms that are not joined up
A compound that contains nitrogen
Two nitrogen atoms joined to each other
A single atom of the element nitrogen

questions.explanation: Yes. N₂ is one molecule made of two nitrogen atoms joined together. Nitrogen gas is an element made of these molecules.

questions.stem: In a sealed tube, 5.6 g of iron reacts completely with 3.2 g of sulfur to make iron sulfide. What mass of iron sulfide is made?
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved: 5.6 g + 3.2 g = 8.8 g, because every atom is still there in the product.

questions.stem: In Dalton's atomic model, how do the atoms of gold compare with the atoms of iron?

options.text: They are the same kind, but packed more tightly
They are the same kind, but gold has more of them
They are yellow and shiny, unlike iron atoms
They are a different kind, with a different mass

questions.explanation: Dalton said all atoms of one element are identical, and differ from the atoms of every other element.

questions.stem: Which of these is a compound?

options.text: Oxygen gas, O₂
Air in a jar
Pure water, H₂O
Salt solution

questions.explanation: Yes. Pure water, H₂O, is a compound: hydrogen and oxygen atoms are chemically joined in a fixed ratio of 2 to 1.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide is CO. Carbon dioxide is CO₂. Which statement is correct?

options.text: They are one compound in different amounts
CO₂ is two CO molecules joined together
Both molecules have the same number of atoms
CO₂ has one more oxygen atom per molecule

questions.explanation: Yes. CO has 1 carbon and 1 oxygen atom; CO₂ has 1 carbon and 2 oxygen atoms. They are different compounds with different, fixed ratios of atoms.

questions.stem: Magnesium is heated in a crucible open to the air until it has all turned into white magnesium oxide. None of the powder escapes. What happens to the mass of the crucible and contents?

options.text: It goes up, as its atoms turn into heavier atoms
It goes down, as some magnesium burns away
It goes up, as oxygen from the air joins on
It stays the same, as oxygen gas has no mass

questions.explanation: Yes. Magnesium joins with oxygen from the air to make magnesium oxide. The crucible is open, so the mass of that oxygen is added to the reading.
